answers.reason: The student representative is elected only at the faculty level and does not hold a university-wide office.
Budget allocation is a central administrative matter where a faculty-level student representative has no seat.
Elected student representatives typically hold a statutory seat on faculty appointment committees to represent student interests in teaching.
As the elected representative of the faculty's students, this person holds a seat on the faculty council.
Student representatives have a core mandate to participate in the study commission advising on teaching and degree programmes.
University regulations normally provide a seat for a student representative on the faculty examination board.
Awarding internal research grants is a research matter where student representatives do not hold a seat.
Rewriting module descriptions for a degree programme directly concerns study matters in which the student representative may participate.
Equipment procurement is an operational and staff decision where student representatives do not have a formal seat.
Planning the orientation week for new students is a faculty student affair in which the elected student representative takes part.
